draft.title: The mental wellbeing continuum
card: Mental wellbeing is not an on and off switch. It can be pictured as a continuum, a line from mentally healthy, through a mental health problem, to a mental health disorder.
Mentally healthy
a person copes with everyday demands and can take part in daily life.
Mental health problem
a person has some distress or difficulty, often linked to a stressor. It affects daily life less than a disorder does and may pass with time or support.
Mental health disorder
a person has a pattern of symptoms that a health professional diagnoses. It is more severe, lasts longer and affects daily life more. A person can move in either direction along the line over time.
draft.remember: Mental wellbeing is a line, not a switch, and a person can move along it in either direction.

a.q: Which statement best fits the idea of a mental wellbeing continuum?
opts: A person's mental wellbeing can shift along a line over time
A person is either mentally healthy or has a disorder
A person who has a disorder will stay at that point for life
A person moves along the line only when they get treatment
a.why: The continuum shows a range, and people can move along it. The statement that a person is either healthy or has a disorder is tempting, but it treats wellbeing as an on and off switch, which the continuum does not.
a.clue: Think of a line, not a switch.

b.q: Priya's grandmother died two months ago. Since then she has felt low and has struggled to focus on homework, but she still goes to school and sees her friends. Her school counsellor sees no diagnosed disorder. Where is Priya best placed on the continuum?
opts: Mental health problem, and she may move back toward healthy
Mental health disorder, because she has felt low for weeks
Mentally healthy, because she still attends school
Mental health problem, and she cannot move from this point
b.why: Priya has distress linked to a stressor and some difficulty, but no diagnosis, and she still takes part in daily life. That fits a mental health problem, and she can move along the line. Calling it a disorder is tempting because of the weeks of low mood, but a disorder is a diagnosed pattern of symptoms that affects daily life more.
b.clue: Is there distress, and is there a diagnosis?
